subject: Additive Effects in F2 intercross cross type

messages.author: d18738ddff11a439
messages.subject: Additive Effects in F2 intercross cross type
parts:
Hi Karl, 
I'm having a bit of difficulty understanding the Additive Effects output. 
 
I'm trying to extract the additive effects of some QTL that I've identified using the stepwise approach (followed by fitQTL() ). 

This is the output I'm getting: 

Estimated effects:
-----------------
                       est       SE      t
Intercept  6.55217  0.29724 22.043
2...@185.0a  0.89848  0.19411  4.629
2...@185.0d -0.08106  0.53421 -0.152
4...@34.8a   1.55674  0.19652  7.922
4...@34.8d   0.52523  0.46044  1.141 

I understand the QTL on 4A  (line -  4...@34.8a) indicates an additive effect of 1.55674.

My questions are:
 
Does this value directly reflect the change in phenotype data between AA and BB allele types? It seems slightly lower than I would expect, judging by comparing the AA vs BB results in the effectplot. Or is it the change in phenotype data between AA and AB, therefore, to work out the difference between AA and BB, I would need to multiply 1.55674 by 2?       

Secondly, if my allele types are: AA, AB, BB - how do I know which allele is having a positive/negative additive effect from this output. 

Thanks for your time!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Additive Effects in F2 intercross cross type
parts:
The additive effect is half the difference between the homozygotes. We take the 2nd genotype minus the first, divided by 2.
If your cross has an "alleles" attribute, that indicates the order of the alleles and so of genotypes.

    data(hyper)
    attr(hyper, "alleles")

The dominance effect is the difference between the heterozygote and the midpoint between the two homozygotes.

karl
